judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A right to renewal ... on the terms then being applied by the Company to similar risks' makes the renewal terms depend on an undefined comparator class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Professional Liability Amendatory Endorsement states the company 'shall not be obligated to renew or continue this policy' (c100), which is difficult to reconcile with an affirmative right of renewal.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No inconsistency identified with the endorsement it introduces.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule of dates and figures with an initial deposit due 02/04/1996 — before the 03/01/1996 inception — and a transcribed amount ('14,0850') that does not fit the pattern.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Condition 1 (c020) treats advance premium as a deposit subject to audit adjustment, and the cancellation clauses (c034, c108) turn on non-payment, so the instalment mechanics interlock with several clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substituted no-action clause is short and clear, though 'full compliance by the insured with all the terms of this policy' is a broad condition precedent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deletes Condition 5 'in its entirety' while the Professional Liability Amendatory says that condition simply 'does not apply' (c098) and the original remains printed (c026) — three positions on one condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only after the insured has been fully compensated for damages' introduces a made-whole test whose measurement is left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the unconditional subrogation right in Condition 7 (c030), which still says the company is subrogated to all the insured's rights on any payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The imputation rule is stated in two sentences with no elastic term beyond 'known to the agent'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Condition 8 (c031) and differs from the near-identical Wisconsin paragraph in c096, which adds the words 'prior to loss'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean statement of the misrepresentation and warranty rules; the terms 'material' and 'contribute to the loss' are standards but familiar ones.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same paragraph is added by c097 in garbled form, and both qualify the reliance/representation language of Condition 12 (c035).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Until there has been a determination that coverage does not exist' does not say by whom or in what forum the determination is made, which controls when the defence duty ends.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the HPL duty to defend and its exhaustion cut-off (c038) and with the no-action clause (c026, c114), so the point at which defence obligations cease must be assembled from several provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The premium-basis definitions are run together and truncated ('sesi' for cost, fragments of remuneration and sales), so several defined terms cannot be read as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These bases feed the CGL schedule and the aggregate-limit subparagraphs keyed to remuneration and receipts (c132, c166), but no substantive conflict is apparent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insuring agreement text is interleaved with exclusion (f) and (g) fragments, so the grant and its qualifications cannot be separated as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The limits it references are replaced by the GL 99 17 amendment (c165-c167) and the persons insured by Form 009-110 (c062); the grant itself is not contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sudden and accidental' in the pollution exception is one of the most heavily litigated phrases in general liability policies, and the text here is additionally run together.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Total Pollution Exclusion (c189-c192) expressly replaces this exclusion while a claims-made Pollution Liability Endorsement (c176-c182) grants pollution cover, so three pollution regimes appear in one policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The war exclusion is intelligible in substance but the transcription merges it with the defence and settlement language of the insuring agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the Premises Medical Payments war exclusion (c145); no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Exclusions (a), (b) and (h) are interleaved on the page, and the liquor exclusion's three-limb structure with a proviso is hard to apply as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (h) is disapplied for host liquor liability (c152) and exclusion (a) is qualified by the extended definition of incidental contract (c010, Broad Form I(A)).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause as printed merges exclusion (d) with fragments of exclusion (k), leaving an incomplete sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (k) is separately replaced by the Broad Form Property Damage coverage (c156); the fragment itself conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The elevator and alienated-premises exclusions run together without their lettering, and 'premises alienated by the named insured' is a term of art.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form Property Damage provision preserves cover 'with respect to the use of elevators' (c156), so the elevator carve-outs must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Loss-of-use exclusion with a 'sudden and accidental' exception — the same phrase that generates disputes elsewhere in the policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with exclusions (n) and (o) (c127, c128) and the property damage definition (c018).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, specific products exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with the products hazard definition as redefined by c195; no clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional 'your work' exclusion, plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form Property Damage Liability Coverage expressly replaces exclusions (k) and (o) (c156), so this printed exclusion no longer stands as written.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sistership exclusion is long but its trigger ('withdrawn from the market or from use because of any known or suspected defect') is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses withdrawal costs; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion operates only where a classification code 'includes the symbol' x, c or u, so its application depends on symbols that the schedule as printed does not display.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The hazard definitions it invokes (c006, c009, c019) are intact, but the CGL schedule of classifications (codes 80613S, 75220 and the like) does not show the symbols the exclusion requires.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long conditional list keyed to how the named insured is designated, with a proviso for mobile equipment operators; detailed but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-110 WI states the persons insured provisions 'are changed to read as follows' (c061, c062), so this printed list is displaced yet remains in the document alongside the Broad Form additions (c161).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An elaborate limits structure with separate aggregates for enumerated categories and a 'continuous or repeated exposure ... one occurrence' rule that parties routinely read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement GL 99 17 amends the 'Limits of Liability' provisions relating to bodily injury and property damage to read differently (c164-c167), so two limits regimes appear in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence tying cover to the defined policy territory; nothing ambiguous in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form Limited Worldwide provision (c160) amends the definition, and the HPL part has its own territory rule as twice amended (c045, c172, c205).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The limit entries are blank and are supplied by default formulas ('Aggregate Limit shall be the per occurrence bodily injury liability limit unless otherwise indicated'), so the personal injury limit must be derived rather than read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declarations state a $1,000,000 occurrence/aggregate CGL limit while endorsement GL 99 17 shows different figures (c164), so the derived personal injury aggregate is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision as printed interleaves the architect/engineer exclusions with the (C) and (D) paragraphs, so the enumerated exclusions cannot be read in sequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (5) of the same set is separately amended by GL 99 19 (c171); no substantive conflict beyond that.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disapplies exclusions identified only as '(0), (c)(2), (a) and (e)', a cross-reference string whose letters are garbled and cannot be matched with confidence to the exclusion list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exclusions it points to (c123, c124) are themselves printed in run-together form, so which contractual-liability exclusions survive is genuinely unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence condition giving the company the insured's rights in arbitration; broad but definite in effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the HPL definition of 'suit' as including arbitration (c047) and the cooperation conditions (c025, c048).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard personal/advertising injury grant tied to 'the conduct of the named insured's business' and the policy territory; broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The offences it covers are defined in c141-c142 as amended by Endorsement No. 3 to add 'Humiliation' (c067), and the limit is the derived figure in c134/c140.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion list numbers two separate paragraphs '(3)', a mechanical numbering error, and the first/knowledge-of-falsity limbs overlap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (1) bars contractually assumed personal injury liability, which sits against the extended incidental contract coverage in the same endorsement (c010, Broad Form I(A)).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear in structure, but it caps liability at 'the limit ... stated in this endorsement as aggregate' where the schedule entry is blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blank is filled only by the default sentence in the Schedule (c134), which equates the aggregate with the per-occurrence bodily injury limit shown in the declarations, requiring a chain of cross-references.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated offence definition ('piracy, unfair competition, or infringement of copyright, title or slogan') whose items are undefined but familiar.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with the advertising injury exclusions in c139; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing carve-out is drafted as a double negative ('except publications ... shall not be deemed personal injury'), obscuring whether it is an exception or an exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3 (c067) amends item (D)1 of this definition to include 'Humiliation', an addition that does not fit the false arrest/detention grouping it is inserted into.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is printed with gaps ('arises out of (a) a condition in the insured [premises] or (b) [operations]'), so the two coverage triggers are incomplete as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its exclusion (D) is deleted by Endorsement No. 8 as misdescribed (c088), materially widening this no-fault medical payments grant for a hospital.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventional vehicle/watercraft/mobile equipment exclusion list with express carve-backs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the CGL exclusions (c123, c124); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated exclusions with an alcohol limb whose 'but only part (a) ... applies when the named insured is such an owner or lessor' proviso is convoluted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Host Liquor endorsement (c152) disapplies exclusion (h) of the CGL but not this medical payments exclusion, a difference that must be respected.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Seven concrete categories of excluded persons; 'any person practicing, instructing or participating in any physical training, sport, athletic activity' is broad but specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the insured premises definition (c149) and the employee exclusions elsewhere; no clash found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence excluding medical expense for services by the named insured or its employees; unambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 8 (c088) purports to delete 'Exclusion (D)' of the Premises Medical Payments Coverage while misdescribing it as Section II, so whether this exclusion survives is genuinely in doubt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An arithmetic limit provision with per person and per accident caps; the final sentence on multiple medical payments coverages is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to 'the limit of bodily injury liability stated in the Policy as applicable to each occurrence', which is itself amended by GL 99 17 (c164-c165).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All premises owned by or rented to the named insured with respect to which the named insured is afforded coverage' is circular but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With many scheduled locations added and deleted by later endorsements (c207, c209, c215, c217), what counts as insured premises shifts through the policy year.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of covered expense types ending with 'funeral services'; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with the deleted exclusion (D) question (c088, c147) but does not itself conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Procedural proof-of-claim and examination requirements, stated definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to but separate from the general notice conditions (c023, c048); no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Functions incidental to the named insured's business' is an elastic qualifier on the liquor carve-back.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies exclusion (h) of the CGL (c123) but leaves the parallel medical payments alcohol exclusion (c145) intact, a deliberate but easily missed asymmetry.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All of the exclusions of the policy, other than the Nuclear Energy Liability Exclusion, are deleted and replaced' is an extraordinarily sweeping sentence whose intended field of operation is not obvious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed $50,000 per occurrence limit with a schedule override; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Schedule entry for Fire Legal Liability is blank (c134), so the default figure governs; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Excess insurance over any valid and collectible property insurance ... such as, but not limited to' uses an illustrative list with an express catch-all, which is at least mildly open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends the Other Insurance Condition (c027), which declares this policy primary, and so must be read with the other excess provisions (c157, c186).

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces CGL exclusions (k) and (o) (c124, c128), which remain printed in the coverage part in their original form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short excess-insurance provision using the same illustrative list formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly amends the Other Insurance Condition (c027) and parallels c155; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: The HPL part states that except as stated there the policy 'does not apply to injury caused by any medical incident' (c050), squarely in tension with a CGL grant of malpractice cover to a hospital insured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second paragraph's sweeping non-contribution language ('no contribution or participation ... on the basis of excess, contributing, deficiency, concurrent, or double insurance or otherwise') is broadly and one-sidedly drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts across the Other Insurance Condition's contribution formulas (c027-c029), which it does not expressly amend.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The added territory limb is numbered '4' though the definition it amends has three paragraphs, and 'permanently domiciled' is left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends the jacket definition (c016) while the HPL part carries its own, twice-amended territory rule (c045, c172, c205).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Ownership or majority interest' and the 90-day cut-off are definite, though the other-insurance proviso is convoluted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule shows an each-occurrence figure larger than the aggregate ($4,000,006 against $1,000,600), an internally impossible pair of limits as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declarations state $1,000,000 each occurrence and $1,000,000 aggregate for CGL, so the endorsement figures that are supposed to control do not match the declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single combined bodily injury/property damage occurrence limit with a financial-responsibility proviso; long but internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the coverage part's separate Coverage A and B limits (c132), which remain printed, and takes its figure from the disputed schedule (c164).
